misfits.why: The -90% is Waymo's any-injury crash rate per mile against a human benchmark; for the DUI group the mechanism is trip substitution by impaired people, which needs the share of impaired trips moved. The mid should not apply to the group's crashes.

misfits.group: bicycle involved | unsafe speed; bicycle involved | not stated
misfits.why: -34% KSI is helmeted against unhelmeted riders. A promotion program changes wearing rates by some points; the program effect is the change in wearing times this, and no take-up figure is given.

misfits.group: pedestrian involved | failure to yield / pedestrian violation
misfits.why: The odds ratio (1.44) is heavy vs light vehicle hazard; the policy effect needs the fleet shift it causes. As written it reads as a policy effect and is a ratio greater than 1 in a field others use for cuts.

misfits.issue: target share beyond the effect's scope
misfits.why: Effect is inside the cell; target share is the whole group (434) because the street-class split was not available. Use the residential share as for the other groups.
The mechanism text says 'not a target'; meta-analyses (Høye 2015, SafetyCube) report rear-end crashes can rise near fixed cameras. Either remove or carry as a possible increase.
Speed cameras do not enforce red; only combined speed/red-light units (Australia) do. Keep only if the record is a combined camera.

misfits.group: vehicles only | unsafe speed; bicycle involved | DUI
misfits.why: Effect is on alcohol-involved fatal crashes; the alcohol share of the speed group is not in results.json, so the record cannot be stacked until it is (results.json can give the 'had been drinking' share).
High -79% (LRSM) is for fatal+injury crashes at rural/suburban sites; the Danish urban figures the lane read give -15% injured and +15% for 3-leg. Use the urban range.

misfits.group: bicycle involved | unsafe turn or lane use (intersection)
misfits.why: Danish +20% all crashes at intersections along new cycle tracks is an increase; a stacking script that treats every effect as a cut will flip it. Pair with protected-intersection or truncated track.

Four conventions: area/crosscut/junction use negative % with low = smallest cut (low > high numerically); bike uses negative % with low = largest cut; speed uses positive '% fewer'; pedestrian uses CMFs. Normalise to one (CMF, low = most protective) before stacking.

red-light-cameras (junction, pedestrian, bike; pedestrian has no cost), protected-left-turn-phase (3 lanes, costs differ), congestion pricing (5 records: area-cordon-congestion-charge, congestion-pricing-cordon $25M-$75M, three 'congestion-pricing' with no cost), LTN (area per cell $250k-$675k vs crosscut and bike per block $6.6k-$75k), citywide-default-20mph (2), ISA (2 each), school-streets (2), superblocks (2), truck-side-guards (2), direct vision (3), no-turn-on-red (2), lower-speed-limits (2), raised-side-street-crossing (2). Merge into one record per fix with all its groups, one unit and one cost.

misfits.fix: group labels that are not size_families rows
misfits.group: vehicles only | crash type Rear End / Hit Object / Overturned; bicycle involved | all families (cross-cut...); pedestrian | 65 and over; pedestrian involved | in the dark
misfits.why: These are crash-type, place or who cuts. Use a prefix scheme ('who | ...', 'place | ...', 'crash type | ...') as the area lane does for place, and give the count from grouping_alternatives.

156 of 173 records name a unit with no number in it (per approach, per corner, per mile) but not how many SF has or how many reach the target group (e.g. SF's signalized intersections, HIN miles, corners on the HIN). The area lane does this (152 cells, 887 unposted miles); the others should.
Keep (filter late) but grade very low; the 32 of 169 drinking-pedestrian crashes is the only basis.
